title: an array spread of a foreign value runs its `Symbol.iterator` exactly as `for…of` does, and is refused for the same reason
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." Spread and `for…of` are the same protocol under two spellings, and `[...x]`, `f(...x)` and `new C(...x)` are one node kind. This case exists beside the `for…of` one on purpose: the defect class kept reopening because each newly noticed sibling was closed at its own site while the siblings nobody thought of stayed silently fail-open. Two cases over one predicate is the cheapest evidence that the answer is total over the grammar rather than a remembered list.
